title: Luke Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Luke 9, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: He called his twelve disciples together
He sent them to preach the kingdom of God
He took the five loaves and two fishes
He asked them, saying, Whom say the people that I am?
questions.correctAnswer: He called his twelve disciples together
questions.explanation: This event occurs first in the chapter, as stated in Luke 9:1.

questions.question: What authority did Jesus give to his disciples?
options: Power and authority over all devils
To preach the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: All of the above
questions.explanation: Jesus gave them power and authority over all devils and to cure diseases, as mentioned in Luke 9:1-2.

questions.question: What did Jesus instruct his disciples to take for their journey?
questions.correctAnswer: Nothing
questions.explanation: Jesus commanded them to take nothing for their journey, as stated in Luke 9:3.

questions.question: Where should the disciples abide when they enter a house?
options: Stay until they leave the city
questions.correctAnswer: Abide there
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed them to abide in whatever house they enter, as noted in Luke 9:4.

questions.question: What should the disciples do if a city does not receive them?
options: Shake off the dust from their feet
questions.correctAnswer: Shake off the dust from their feet
questions.explanation: Jesus told them to shake off the very dust from their feet as a testimony against those who do not receive them, according to Luke 9:5.

questions.question: What did the apostles do after they returned from their journey?
options: They went back to their homes
They told Jesus all that they had done
questions.correctAnswer: They told Jesus all that they had done
questions.explanation: The apostles returned and reported to Jesus all that they had accomplished during their journey, as mentioned in Luke 9:10.

questions.question: How many men were present when the disciples were asked to feed the multitude?
questions.correctAnswer: Five thousand
questions.explanation: The text states that there were about five thousand men present, as noted in Luke 9:14.

questions.question: What did Jesus do with the five loaves and two fishes?
options: He gave them to the crowd directly
He blessed them and broke them
questions.correctAnswer: He blessed them and broke them
questions.explanation: Jesus took the five loaves and two fishes, looking up to heaven, He blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples, as stated in Luke 9:16.

questions.question: What was collected after everyone had eaten?
questions.correctAnswer: Twelve baskets of fragments
questions.explanation: After everyone had eaten, twelve baskets of fragments were collected, as mentioned in Luke 9:17.

questions.question: What did Jesus ask his disciples while he was alone praying?
options: Whom say ye that I am?
What do you think of the people?
questions.correctAnswer: Whom say ye that I am?
questions.explanation: Jesus asked his disciples, Whom say the people that I am? while he was alone praying, as stated in Luke 9:18.

questions.question: What was Peter's response to Jesus' question about who he was?
options: He is the Christ of God
questions.correctAnswer: He is the Christ of God
questions.explanation: Peter answered Jesus by saying, The Christ of God, as noted in Luke 9:20.

questions.question: Did Jesus command the disciples to tell others that he was the Christ?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Jesus straitly charged them and commanded them to tell no man that he was the Christ, as stated in Luke 9:21.

questions.question: Did the disciples heal the sick as they preached?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The disciples went through the towns preaching the gospel and healing everywhere, as mentioned in Luke 9:6.

questions.question: Herod was pleased with all that was done by Jesus.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Herod was perplexed by all that was done and desired to see Jesus, indicating he was not pleased, as stated in Luke 9:7-9.

questions.question: The multitude followed Jesus because they wanted to argue with him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The people followed Jesus because they knew he received them and spoke to them of the kingdom of God, as stated in Luke 9:11.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What must the Son of man suffer according to Luke 9:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Rejection and death
questions.explanation: Luke 9:22 states that the Son of man must suffer many things, be rejected, and be slain.

questions.question: What does Luke 9:24 promise will happen if someone loses their life for Jesus' sake?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be saved
questions.explanation: Luke 9:24 indicates that whosoever will lose his life for Christ’s sake shall save it.

questions.question: According to Luke 9:25, what is the disadvantage of gaining the whole world?
questions.correctAnswer: It results in losing oneself
questions.explanation: Luke 9:25 asks what advantage a man has if he gains the world but loses himself.

questions.question: In Luke 9:26, what will happen to those who are ashamed of Jesus?
options: The Son of man will be ashamed of them
questions.correctAnswer: The Son of man will be ashamed of them
questions.explanation: Luke 9:26 states that whosoever is ashamed of Jesus and his words, he will be ashamed of them when he comes in glory.

questions.question: What significant event does Jesus mention in Luke 9:27?
options: Some will taste death before seeing the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: Some will taste death before seeing the kingdom of God
questions.explanation: Luke 9:27 mentions that some standing there would not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.

questions.question: According to Luke 9:29, what happened to Jesus while he prayed?
options: He was filled with the Spirit
questions.correctAnswer: His appearance changed
questions.explanation: Luke 9:29 describes how the fashion of his countenance was altered while he prayed.

questions.question: What was discussed by Moses and Elias with Jesus in Luke 9:31?
questions.correctAnswer: His decease at Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Luke 9:31 states that Moses and Elias spoke of Jesus' decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Luke 9:32, what caused Peter and the others to see Jesus' glory?
questions.correctAnswer: Their awakening
questions.explanation: Luke 9:32 explains that when Peter and those with him were awake, they saw his glory and the two men with him.

questions.question: What does Peter suggest in Luke 9:33?
questions.correctAnswer: To make three tabernacles
questions.explanation: In Luke 9:33, Peter suggests making three tabernacles for Jesus, Moses, and Elias.

questions.question: What does the voice from the cloud declare in Luke 9:35?
options: This is my beloved Son: hear him
questions.correctAnswer: This is my beloved Son: hear him
questions.explanation: The voice from the cloud in Luke 9:35 identifies Jesus as God's beloved Son and instructs to hear Him.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the faithless generation in Luke 9:41?
options: How long shall I be with you?
questions.correctAnswer: How long shall I be with you?
questions.explanation: In Luke 9:41, Jesus expresses frustration by asking how long he must be with and suffer the faithless generation.

questions.question: What was the outcome after Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit in Luke 9:42?
questions.correctAnswer: The child was healed
questions.explanation: Luke 9:42 states that Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the child, and delivered him to his father.

questions.question: Is it true that Jesus taught that one must deny oneself and take up their cross daily?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Luke 9:23 shows Jesus teaching that anyone who wishes to follow him must deny themselves and take up their cross daily.

questions.question: Is it false that those who are ashamed of Jesus will be rewarded?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: It is false because Luke 9:26 says that whosoever is ashamed of Jesus will be ashamed by him when he comes in glory.

questions.question: Is it false that Peter suggested making one tabernacle for Jesus?
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: It is false because Luke 9:33 reveals that Peter actually suggested making three tabernacles.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 9.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about whoever receives a child in His name in Luke 9:48?
options: Receiveth me, and receiveth him that sent me
questions.correctAnswer: Receiveth me, and receiveth him that sent me
questions.explanation: Luke 9:48 explicitly states that whoever receives the child in Jesus' name receives Him, and whoever receives Him receives the One who sent Him.

questions.question: In Luke 9:50, Jesus responds to John about forbidding someone casting out devils in His name. What reason does Jesus give?
options: He that is not against us is for us
Only the twelve can cast out devils
questions.correctAnswer: He that is not against us is for us
questions.explanation: Luke 9:50 records Jesus telling John not to forbid the man because anyone not opposing them is considered to be for them.

questions.question: What was the disciples’ reaction to the Samaritan village not receiving Jesus in Luke 9:54?
options: They asked to call down fire from heaven
questions.correctAnswer: They asked to call down fire from heaven
questions.explanation: In Luke 9:54, James and John asked Jesus if they should command fire to come down from heaven to consume the Samaritans, showing their zeal influenced by Elijah's example.

questions.question: What reason does Jesus give in Luke 9:56 for not coming to destroy lives but to save them?
options: For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them
For the kingdom of God is peace
For the prophets have spoken peace
questions.correctAnswer: For the Son of man is not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them
questions.explanation: Luke 9:56 records Jesus rebuking His disciples and explaining His mission is salvation, not destruction.

questions.question: In Luke 9:44, to what does Jesus warn His disciples to pay attention?
options: The sayings that the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men
The coming of the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: The sayings that the Son of man shall be delivered into the hands of men
questions.explanation: Luke 9:44 clearly states Jesus telling His disciples to let these sayings sink into their ears because He will be delivered into men’s hands.

questions.question: What did Jesus do when He perceived the disciples' reasoning about who should be greatest in Luke 9:47?
options: He took a child and set him by Him
He called for a public debate
questions.correctAnswer: He took a child and set him by Him
questions.explanation: Luke 9:47 states Jesus, perceiving their thoughts, took a child and set him by Himself to teach humility and greatness.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'parakaleo' in Luke 9:23 mean?
options: To call near, to exhort or urge
questions.correctAnswer: To call near, to exhort or urge
questions.explanation: 'Parakaleo' (παρακαλέω) in Luke 9:23 means to call near or to exhort, which fits Jesus' urging people to deny themselves and follow Him.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Luke 9:23-24 where Jesus talks about denying oneself and taking up the cross?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Luke 9:23-24 uses chiasm, a literary structure where ideas are presented and then repeated in reverse order to emphasize the paradox of losing life to save it.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of Jesus being delivered into the hands of men as in Luke 9:44?
questions.correctAnswer: Psalm 22:16
questions.explanation: Psalm 22:16 foreshadows the suffering and being delivered into the hands of men, connecting with Jesus’ prediction in Luke 9:44.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the prophecy of suffering and being rejected referenced in Luke 9:22?
questions.correctAnswer: Acts 3:18
questions.explanation: Acts 3:18 references the fulfillment of Jesus' suffering and rejection as predicted in Luke 9:22.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus telling His disciples to take up their cross daily in Luke 9?
options: Peter's confession that Jesus is the Christ of God
The feeding of the five thousand
The healing of the demon-possessed boy
Jesus predicting His death and resurrection
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus predicting His death and resurrection
questions.explanation: Luke 9:22 immediately precedes the call to deny oneself and take up the cross in 9:23, as Jesus predicts His suffering and resurrection.

questions.question: How does the concept of 'kingdom of God' in Luke 9:60 connect with Jewish eschatological expectations?
options: It reflects the urgent call to proclaim God's reign despite social obligations
It symbolizes a physical kingdom with political power
It means strict adherence to the Mosaic Law
It refers to the temple rituals
questions.correctAnswer: It reflects the urgent call to proclaim God's reign despite social obligations
questions.explanation: Luke 9:60’s instruction to 'go and preach the kingdom of God' emphasizes the priority of God's reign over traditional social duties, a key theme in Jewish eschatology.

questions.question: What typological significance can be drawn from Jesus taking a child in Luke 9:47 in the context of first-century Jewish culture?
options: Children represented humility and dependence, contrasting with disciples’ ambition
Children were seen as leaders in society
questions.correctAnswer: Children represented humility and dependence, contrasting with disciples’ ambition
questions.explanation: In Luke 9:47, Jesus uses a child, culturally seen as low status and dependent, to teach that true greatness is humility, contrasting with the disciples’ ambition.

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 9:62, Jesus said a man looking back after putting his hand to the plough is fit for the kingdom of God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 9:62 clearly states that no man looking back after putting his hand to the plough is fit for the kingdom of God, making the statement false.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 9:45 states the disciples understood fully when Jesus said He would be delivered into the hands of men.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Luke 9:45 explains that the disciples did not understand Jesus’ statement about being delivered; it was hidden from them.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 9:22 teach about the nature of salvation?
options: Salvation requires Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection
Salvation is based solely on human effort and obedience
Salvation is granted through earthly power and influence
Salvation is achieved through ritual and sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation requires Christ's suffering, death, and resurrection
questions.explanation: Luke 9:22 states that the Son of man must suffer, be rejected, be slain, and be raised on the third day, thus teaching salvation comes through Christ's sacrificial death and resurrection.

questions.question: What doctrine about discipleship and sanctification is taught in Luke 9:23?
options: True discipleship involves self-denial and daily cross-bearing
Discipleship is about gaining worldly success and comfort
Following Christ requires occasional sacrifices only
Sanctification is instantaneous and requires no ongoing effort
questions.correctAnswer: True discipleship involves self-denial and daily cross-bearing
questions.explanation: Luke 9:23 teaches that to follow Christ, one must deny self, take up the cross daily, and follow Him, indicating ongoing sanctification involves self-denial and perseverance.

questions.question: What doctrine about the kingdom of God is taught in Luke 9:2?
options: The kingdom of God is proclaimed alongside healing and restoration
The kingdom of God is only a future, spiritual reality
The kingdom of God is a political kingdom to overthrow rulers
The kingdom of God is restricted to the Jewish people only
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom of God is proclaimed alongside healing and restoration
questions.explanation: Luke 9:2 states the disciples were sent to preach the kingdom of God and heal the sick, teaching the kingdom involves both proclamation and tangible restoration.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 9:35 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Divine Sonship
questions.explanation: Luke 9:35 records God’s voice declaring Jesus as 'my beloved Son,' demonstrating the attribute of divine sonship.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Luke 9:41 when Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty over evil
questions.explanation: In Luke 9:41, Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit and heals the boy, demonstrating His sovereign power over evil spirits.

questions.question: How does Luke 9:51-56 prepare for the theme of Jesus’ passion and rejection elsewhere in Scripture?
options: It anticipates Jesus’ rejection by the Samaritans as a foreshadowing of His rejection in Jerusalem
It shows Jesus’ triumph over all His enemies without suffering
It emphasizes Jesus’ political power to punish those who reject Him
It suggests Jesus avoids conflict by not confronting rejection
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates Jesus’ rejection by the Samaritans as a foreshadowing of His rejection in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Luke 9:53-54 shows Jesus rejected by Samaritans, foreshadowing the greater rejection He will face in Jerusalem, connecting to the passion narrative.

questions.question: How does the transfiguration account in Luke 9:28-36 connect to Old Testament revelation?
options: It reveals Jesus’ fulfillment of the Law and Prophets through the presence of Moses and Elijah
It introduces a new covenant without connection to the Old Testament
It denies the authority of the Law and Prophets
It focuses solely on Jesus’ human nature without divine confirmation
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals Jesus’ fulfillment of the Law and Prophets through the presence of Moses and Elijah
questions.explanation: Luke 9:30-31 shows Moses and Elijah talking with Jesus about His death, revealing Jesus as fulfillment of the Law and Prophets.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 9:23 and Luke 9:24 teach about discipleship and eternal life?
options: Discipleship requires self-denial and cross-bearing, leading to true life by losing one’s life for Christ
Discipleship guarantees worldly success and prosperity
Eternal life is earned by avoiding suffering and hardship
Self-preservation is the highest goal of discipleship
questions.correctAnswer: Discipleship requires self-denial and cross-bearing, leading to true life by losing one’s life for Christ
questions.explanation: Luke 9:23 teaches self-denial and cross-bearing as discipleship marks, and Luke 9:24 teaches that losing one’s life for Christ’s sake results in saving it, linking discipleship with eternal life.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 9:20 and Luke 9:26 teach about Christ’s identity and eschatological glory?
options: Jesus is the Christ of God whose eschatological coming will be accompanied by glory with the Father and angels
Jesus is only a prophet with no future eschatological role
Jesus’ identity is secret and never revealed to His disciples
Jesus will return in humility without glory or divine accompaniment
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus is the Christ of God whose eschatological coming will be accompanied by glory with the Father and angels
questions.explanation: Luke 9:20 confesses Jesus as the Christ, and 9:26 promises that the Son of man will come in His own glory and the Father’s, with angels, revealing His eschatological glory.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth is taught by Luke 9:49-50 regarding ministry and unity?
options: Ministry done in Jesus’ name by those not part of the immediate group is still valid and unity is to be maintained
Only the twelve disciples have authority to minister in Jesus’ name
Ministry outside the apostles is invalid and divisive
Unity is less important than doctrinal purity
questions.correctAnswer: Ministry done in Jesus’ name by those not part of the immediate group is still valid and unity is to be maintained
questions.explanation: Luke 9:49-50 shows Jesus instructing not to forbid someone casting out devils in His name because 'he that is not against us is for us,' teaching unity and broad validity of ministry.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Jesus’ instruction in Luke 9:58 about having no place to lay His head shows He was homeless and powerless. What does Luke 9:58 actually teach?
options: It teaches Jesus embraced poverty and homelessness as part of discipleship
It proves Jesus was rejected and abandoned with no support
It shows Jesus lacked divine provision and protection
It indicates Jesus' ministry was unsuccessful and marginalized
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches Jesus embraced poverty and homelessness as part of discipleship
questions.explanation: Luke 9:58 illustrates Jesus’ voluntary acceptance of a homeless, itinerant lifestyle as a mark of discipleship, not weakness or divine abandonment.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 9:27 teach concerning eschatology and the kingdom of God?
options: Some standing with Jesus will see the kingdom of God before death
The kingdom of God is only a future event after death
The kingdom of God is purely spiritual with no visible manifestation
Eschatological promises are for future generations only
questions.correctAnswer: Some standing with Jesus will see the kingdom of God before death
questions.explanation: Luke 9:27 states some present will not taste death before seeing the kingdom of God, teaching an inaugurated eschatology with partial fulfillment in Jesus’ lifetime.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Luke 9:44 where Jesus predicts His betrayal?
questions.correctAnswer: Omniscience
questions.explanation: Luke 9:44 shows Jesus foreknowing He will be delivered into men’s hands, demonstrating His omniscience.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal truth do Luke 9:46-48 reveal about humility and the nature of greatness in the kingdom of God?
options: True greatness is found in receiving the least, like a child, and humility precedes exaltation
Greatness is achieved through power and dominance over others
Exalting oneself is the path to greatness
Children are excluded from the kingdom of God
questions.correctAnswer: True greatness is found in receiving the least, like a child, and humility precedes exaltation
questions.explanation: Luke 9:47-48 teaches that receiving a child in Jesus’ name is receiving Him, and that the least shall be greatest, highlighting humility as central to kingdom greatness.

questions.question: How does Luke 9:3-5 teach about reliance on divine providence and the nature of mission?
options: Disciples are to depend fully on God’s provision without worldly preparations
Mission requires extensive planning and material resources
Success comes through financial security and self-sufficiency
Disciples should avoid confrontation by retreating when rejected
questions.correctAnswer: Disciples are to depend fully on God’s provision without worldly preparations
questions.explanation: Luke 9:3-5 instructs disciples to take nothing for the journey and to shake dust off where not received, emphasizing reliance on God’s provision and the seriousness of mission.
